note: Mills County Conservation park near Glenwood on the Loess Hills Scenic Byway; the county conservation office and two rental cabins are in the park. The one water hydrant is by the playground in the small electric loop. The 82-acre Pony Creek Lake is across the road from the park entrance, about 400 m west of the loop. April-November. --Claude
summary: The county's camping page confirms 4 first-come electric sites (50/30A) on ~40x30 ft gravel pads, $20/day self-registration, 14-day limit, pit toilets, no showers or dump, one shared hydrant. Phone 712-527-9685 (conservation office in the park) found. Not waterfront stands; pin OK.

STALE COUNTY PDF: the county's own 'Pony Creek Park (PDF)' park sheet still says 6 electric sites (50/30/20A) on 14x~30 ft pads at $12; the camping page (4 sites, 40x30 ft pads, $20) is the current one and was used.
SEASON: the note's 'April-November' is not stated on any county page I read; kept as note text, no season written.

WATERFRONT: 'not waterfront' confirmed. On Esri imagery the electric loop (gravel pull-ins with an RV on the west side, playground in the middle, ~41.0729,-95.7849) sits in woods at the end of the park road; the 82-acre lake is ~400 m west across Deacon Rd.
PIN: stored 41.07254,-95.78488 is at the loop's entry junction, ~60 m south of the pads. OK.
